extracted.intended_audience: public relations instructors, curriculum designers, and assessment researchers (academics and PR professionals involved in teaching/assessing PR writing)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, teaching, and measuring students' public relations news-release writing skills using iterative improvement and validated scoring rubrics developed with practitioner input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply Deming's PDCA Cycle for continuous improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ Deming's PDCA (Plan-Do-Check-Act) Cycle as a systematic procedure to incrementally move closer to the goal of valid and reliable teaching and assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a multiyear, iterative process (plan interventions, implement, evaluate outcomes, and adjust) rather than relying on ad-hoc trial-and-error; treat assessment development as continuous improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify basic SKAs for career-ready graduates
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the basic skills, knowledge, and abilities (SKAs) that constitute a career-ready graduate in public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather these SKAs through structured input from public relations professionals and stakeholders so that learning targets align with employer expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orient pedagogy to career-specific needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide how to orient instructional approaches and curriculum to prepare students for identified career-specific SKAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate consensus between academics and practitioners on pedagogy so teaching methods reflect real-world professional needs and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a repeatable, reliable rubric for news-release writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a scoring rubric that reliably measures students' news release writing skills and can be applied consistently across cohorts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the rubric to be repeatable and reliable; use iterative testing and refinement (including inter-rater checks) to ensure consistent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure validity of assessment measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Attend to the validity of the measurements used to evaluate student learning—i.e., confirm the rubric measures the intended SKAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ methods (qualitative and quantitative) to validate the rubric, including content validity via practitioner consensus and statistical analyses to examine measurement properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mixed qualitative and quantitative procedures to develop assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a variety of qualitative and quantitative procedures in the development and validation of pedagogy and assessment tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include practitioner interviews/surveys, consensus-building techniques (e.g., Delphi), rubric pilot testing, and statistical analysis of scores; combine methods to strengthen evidence for decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate with public relations professionals in assessment design
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage public relations practitioners in gathering information and facilitating consensus to ensure assessments reflect professional practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use practitioner input to define SKAs, prioritize rubric criteria, and review assessment tools so they are meaningful and defensible to employers and the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus assessment specifically on news-release writing skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Target the rubric and instructional assessment specifically at news release (press-release) writing skills as a distinct, measurable competency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design criterion descriptors and performance levels that capture elements of news-release writing (e.g., lead, newsworthiness, accuracy, clarity, structure, AP-style conventions) though the page notes the general aim rather than listing each element.
